title: The training and promotion settings
description: Every threshold the training pipeline branches on, fixed in a contract rather than as constants in pipelines/ml/. A promotion gate whose threshold lives in the module it gates is a dial the same session can turn until the model passes, which is the shape docs/DECISIONS.md refused for the inference settings and refuses again here. Every entry is a {value, source} pair; nothing in this file is law, so every source is a scenario_assumption. NOTE what this file deliberately does NOT carry: a price response. On this repository's corpus price is a deterministic function of hours-to-expiry within an arm, so no price response is identified from history and none is declared here — see pipelines/ml/__init__.py and docs/FINDINGS.md.

split.description: How history is divided. Time-based, never random: a random split lets a Tuesday in the evaluation half be predicted from the Wednesday after it, which is the future leaking into training through the split itself.

evaluation_days.description: How many trailing business dates are held out for evaluation. The split point is derived from this and from the data's own last date; it is never chosen after the numbers are seen.

min_training_days.description: The fewest distinct business dates a model may be fitted on. Below this the fit is refused rather than produced with a wide interval nobody reads.

reconstruction.description: What claim 4's correction is allowed to contribute to a training set.

min_observed_share.description: The smallest share of an ordinary day a censored store-day's observed window may cover and still be used as a demand observation. Sourced from ARITHMETIC rather than from an error measurement, deliberately: the reconstruction is at_least / share, so `share` is exactly the fraction of the answer that is evidence and 1 - share is the fraction that is curve. A measured error threshold would have to come from evals/censoring/, whose censoring is constructed on ordinary days, and docs/DECISIONS.md refuses that as the wrong distribution for a live guard.

gates.description: What a model must satisfy before a human may be asked to approve it. Doctrine rule 5: nothing approves itself, so passing every gate here grants nothing — it only makes an approval possible.

calibration_tolerance_pct.description: How far the total predicted units may sit from the total observed units, over the evaluation half, as a percentage of observed. This is the gate ABOVE RMSE: a model that is systematically optimistic by 20% sets systematically low prices, and every individual price still passes every guardrail.

rmse_share_of_baseline.description: The largest share of the do-nothing baseline's RMSE that will be admitted, where the baseline predicts the training grand rate for every store-SKU-day. Kept beside calibration because calibration alone passes a model that is unbiased and useless — the baseline itself is perfectly calibrated by construction, and this is the gate that refuses it. Expressed as a share rather than in units because a ceiling in units has to know the scale of demand, which is a property of the corpus and not of the model.

segment_family_false_alarm_rate.description: The probability that the per-segment calibration gate refuses a WELL-CALIBRATED model on a given run, over all the segments it judges. The per-segment limit is derived from this and from how many segments were judged — a Bonferroni correction — rather than declared as a fixed multiple of a standard error, because the same multiple means different things over twenty-one segments and over two hundred. This is the number that tells the next person whether a red run is real, so it is the number that is declared and the limit is what is computed.

min_segment_days.description: The fewest evaluation store-SKU-days a segment must carry before its calibration is judged. A segment with three days produces a percentage that swings on one shopper, and judging it would be reading noise as a defect.
